transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I guess what finally made me agree to come in is that... I just don't care about the things that used to keep me balanced anymore. 

Things like sailing races, my Saturday shift at the historical society, or even just tinkering out in the woodshop. Lately, they all just feel like chores, and I just keep putting them off. It didn't seem right to just stop doing everything I enjoy, so here I am.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?
No, I wouldn't say I feel sad or down. It's more like... I just feel flat. There's no real sadness, just a lack of interest in everything.
How long have you been feeling this lack of interest in the things you used to enjoy?
Well, I'd say it's been a little over a year now. Basically, this has all been going on since the scaffold accident we had at work during the business readjustment.
Do you still enjoy things like eating or spending time with friends and family?

Not really. I mean, my wife and kids can be laughing at dinner, or I can finally finish a difficult project milestone at work... and I know those things should feel good. But mostly, I just feel flat and a little removed from it all.
Do you often feel guilty about anything?

Yeah, I do. It's... well, there's this constant, low-grade dread and guilt that just kind of follows me around now. I keep feeling like I should have seen one more risk coming with that scaffold. People keep telling me the safety controls were all in place and there was nothing else to be done, but... I still just can't shake that feeling.
Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or ending your life?
No, no I haven't. I mean, I feel pretty down and stuck in my head a lot of the time, but... no, I haven't had any thoughts about hurting myself or ending my life. It's just not like that.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?
No, I haven't. My weight has stayed pretty much the same. I haven't really noticed any changes there.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level or how active you are compared to before?

Not really, no. I mean, I still get up and go to work, and do what I need to do. I might feel a little drained sometimes just from being so stuck in my head, but... my actual energy levels and how active I am haven't really changed. I'm still keeping up with my normal routine.
Have you been having any trouble sleeping lately?

Well, yeah, a little bit. I mean, most nights I can actually get to bed at a reasonable hour, but... I always seem to wake up around two or three in the morning. My mind just goes right back to that job site. And then I'm just lying there, wide awake, listening for every little sound instead of actually getting any real rest. So, yeah, sleep hasn't been great.
Do you find yourself moving or speaking more slowly than you used to?
No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I mean, I still move and talk at my usual pace. Nobody at work has pointed anything out either, so... no, no changes there.
Do you often feel worthless or like you're not a good person?

No, I don't feel like that. I mean, I know I'm a decent guy and I do my job well. I don't really sit around feeling worthless or anything. It's just... well, like I said, it's mostly just dealing with my head getting stuck on that job site and the lack of sleep. But as far as feeling like a bad person? No, I don't have that going on.
Do you find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless more often than you used to?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I might be a little tired during the day from waking up so much, but I'm not... pacing around or fidgeting. I can sit at my desk and do my work just fine. So, no, no real restlessness.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating or making decisions?

No, my concentration is fine. I mean, I manage my projects at work without any issues, and I don't have trouble making decisions. Sometimes I'm a bit groggy from the bad sleep, but once I'm at my desk, I can focus just like always.
Do you think you've been more lethargic or sluggish in your movements lately?

No, not really. I mean, I'm definitely tired from the lack of sleep, but I wouldn't say I'm sluggish or moving slower than usual. I still get up, get ready, and go about my day at a normal pace. It's just the being tired part, not really a physical slowness.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or agitated, like you can't sit still?

No, I don't get that feeling. I think we touched on this a bit earlier, but... no, I don't feel agitated or jittery. I have no problem sitting still at my desk to get my work done. It really is just being tired, not anxious.
Do you feel like you're reacting more slowly to things than you used to?
No, I wouldn't say that. I react to things just fine. Like I said, I'm just tired, but my reflexes and how I respond to things around me seem completely normal.
Do you think other people have noticed you moving or speaking more slowly than usual?

No, nobody has said anything to me about it. I work with a lot of the same people every day, and... well, I'm pretty sure someone would point it out if I was dragging or talking slower than normal. So, no, I haven't had anyone notice anything like that.
Would you say this lack of interest and feeling flat is something that's affecting your daily life most of the day, nearly every day?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I don't really feel flat or... or like I've lost interest in things. I still care about my projects at work and what's going on around me. It's definitely not an all-day, every day kind of thing where I just don't care. Like I was saying, it really just comes down to being tired, not... not a lack of interest.
Would you say this feeling of flatness and lack of interest is mild, or is it significantly impacting your ability to function?

Well, like I just said, I don't really feel flat or disinterested. But as far as how things are impacting my ability to function... I guess you could say it's mild, but I am noticing it at work. I mean, I’m still doing my job. But I’ve started delegating site visits that I really should be leading myself. And... I find myself avoiding client discussions if they happen to touch on the accident. It makes me worry a bit that I’m not giving the project the steady direction it needs.
How long have you been noticing a lack of interest in the things you used to enjoy, such as sailing races and working at the historical society?

Well, like I said, I wouldn't really call it a lack of interest in things. But as far as everything else... this has all been going on since the scaffold accident. That happened during the business readjustment, so... I guess it's been a little over a year now.
